headline: Sales grow, GAAP margins compress, guidance raised
summary_short: Hubbell's Q2 2026 net sales rose 15% y/y to $1.71B (organic +10%), while GAAP diluted EPS fell 1% to $4.52 as GAAP operating margin compressed 230bp on acquisition-related costs; adjusted diluted EPS rose 12% to $5.52.
summary_long: Net sales rose 15% y/y to $1.71B, with 10% organic growth (Electrical +18%, Utility +6%) plus the ~$3.0B NSI Industries acquisition closed in the quarter. GAAP operating margin fell 230bp to 20.4% as acquisition amortization and transaction/integration costs rose sharply; adjusted operating margin held closer, down 50bp to 23.9%. Interest expense nearly tripled to $39.1M on new NSI-related debt (a $900M term loan plus $1.9B of senior notes), pushing GAAP net income down 2% to $240.4M and diluted EPS down 1% to $4.52, while adjusted diluted EPS rose 12% to $5.52. Free cash flow was $212.8M. Hubbell raised full-year 2026 guidance: adjusted EPS to $20.25-$20.55 and its organic sales outlook, plus GAAP EPS of $17.25-$17.55.

drivers.explanation: CEO Gerben Bakker attributed the quarter's results to double-digit gains across sales, adjusted operating profit, and adjusted EPS, crediting strong positioning in utility and electrical end markets plus disciplined inflation management via pricing and productivity.

Company cites demand from grid modernization, load growth, and datacenter investment as driving the quarter's organic growth, plus incremental net sales from the newly closed NSI Industries acquisition.
Electrical Solutions organic net sales grew 18% on volume and favorable price/productivity, while Utility Solutions organic net sales grew about 6%, per segment results.
Cost of goods sold grew about 18% y/y, outpacing 15% net sales growth, which mechanically compresses gross margin even before considering any single disclosed driver.

Utility Solutions and Electrical Solutions segment operating income both grew, driven by volume growth, the NSI acquisition, and favorable price/productivity, partially offset by cost inflation, raw material costs and tariffs.

GAAP operating margin fell 230bp as acquisition-related intangible amortization rose to $39.1M (from $25.2M) and transaction/integration/separation costs rose to $28.0M (from $0.7M), both tied to the NSI Industries acquisition.

Electrical Solutions adjusted operating margin fell 130bp on inflation, raw material costs, tariffs and restructuring investment, more than offsetting Utility Solutions' +10bp adjusted margin gain from favorable price and productivity.
EPS decline of about 1% is arithmetically consistent with net income falling roughly 2% against a nearly flat, slightly lower diluted share count (53.1M vs 53.5M).

Adjusted net income rose 11% as higher adjusted operating income (up 13% to $408.5M) outpaced the larger addbacks for acquisition amortization and NSI-related transaction/integration/separation costs excluded from GAAP.
Interest expense nearly tripled to $39.1M from $14.5M after Hubbell funded the roughly $3.0B NSI Industries acquisition with a new $900M term loan, $1.9B of senior notes, and commercial paper.
